Hi Oliver — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the handful of operational questions your security team raised so we can keep the procurement motion moving.

Highlights from the demo that matter for the follow-ups:
- Data at-rest: Redwood uses AES-256-GCM for model checkpoints and customer payloads by default.
- In-transit: mutual TLS for control plane + TLS1.2+ for data plane; option for mTLS on customer-facing endpoints.
- KMS: Hosted (Redwood-managed), Dedicated KMS integration (customer CMK via AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault), and a BYOHSM option (we can integrate with CloudHSM vendors or on-prem HSM proxies).

Your security questions were: key ownership/rotation, ability to use FIPS/HSM-backed keys, access/audit logs retention, and whether keys are exportable. Can you confirm folks on your side who should be in the thread for technical answers? I copied Aditya (security engineering) and Monica (solutions).

Action items I suggest:
1) Oliver: confirm which KMS model Clearbank prefers (Hosted KMS | Customer-Managed KMS | On-prem HSM).
2) Security: send the top 3 compliance must-haves (e.g., FIPS level, non-exportability, rotation cadence).
3) Redwood (Aditya): provide a short operational matrix that maps each KMS option to guarantees (key custody, rotation, audit log retention, required network connectivity).

Attaching a one-pager that summarizes the options and a template you can drop your requirements into.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up call if helpful.

—

Hi Soojin — thanks for the concise recap and the doc. A few clarifications from Clearbank security (I'll keep it short):

1) Key ownership: we need customer-managed keys (CMK) for production. Hosted KMS is acceptable for POCs only.
2) HSM requirement: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent for private keys used to unwrap data encryption keys.
3) Non-exportability: keys used for unwrapping must be non-exportable.
4) Rotation: 90-day rotation for wrapping keys is our baseline; monthly rotation for session keys is fine.
5) Audit logs: retention for 7 years; logs must show key usage with timestamp, principal, and operation.
6) Residency: EU data must remain in EU regions; KMS should be in same region where possible.

Two follow-up questions we couldn't get to in the demo: 
- Can Redwood provide a pull-based audit export (S3 or syslog) with SHA-256 integrity markers?
- For the BYOHSM model, does Redwood require a VPN or can we expose an internal HSM gateway over mutual TLS?

If Aditya can answer the two technical follow-ups that would be great. We can then share an internal checklist back to you.

Thanks,
Oliver
Chief Security Officer
Clearbank Technologies

> 3) Non-exportability: keys used for unwrapping must be non-exportable.

> 6) Residency: EU data must remain in EU regions; KMS should be in same region where possible.

Thanks for the clear asks — quick technical answers and constraints from Redwood side below.

Short answers:
- CMK support: yes. We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Google Cloud KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. For on-prem HSMs we support a gateway approach where the HSM exposes a PKCS#11 or KMIP interface behind a customer-managed proxy.
- FIPS/HSM: we can integrate with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs via CloudHSM or partner appliances. For hosted Redwood-managed KMS we use FIPS-validated providers; for BYOHSM the HSM is customer-controlled and must meet your reqs.
- Non-exportability: for AWS KMS/Azure you can configure non-exportable keys; for KMIP/PKCS#11 HSMs keys are non-exportable by default when generated on-device.
- Rotation: Redwood supports automated key rotation policies but we currently rely on customer KMS controls for CMK rotation. For wrapping keys generated by Redwood we can set a 90-day rotation cadence.
- Audit logs: we can stream key usage logs to a customer-owned S3/Blob location or push to a syslog endpoint. Logs include timestamp, principal (service account/role), operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign/Verify), key-id, and request id. We can add SHA-256 digests to exported batches for integrity.
- Residency: we can pin KMS endpoints and storage to an EU region; for model serving we route requests to EU capacity.

Operational constraints and notes:
- BYOHSM network: recommended pattern is to expose a customer HSM gateway reachable over mTLS from Redwood's private peering/VPC. We can also support a VPN or direct connect if customers prefer. Exposing HSM over public internet is not recommended unless behind a firewall and mTLS + IP allowlist.
- Latency: calling an external KMS/HSM on every token generation adds ~5-20ms per call depending on network path; we use envelope encryption and local wrapping-key caches to keep per-token latency low.
- Key rotation impact: if you rotate a wrapping CMK, make sure old ciphertexts still have a readable key-encryption-key (we support key versioning and rewrap workflows to avoid data loss).

Next steps I propose:
- Aditya: draft the operational matrix (matrix will include: option, custody, rotation responsibility, audit export method, connectivity, avg added latency). I'll send that by EOD.
- Oliver: confirm preferred connectivity model for BYOHSM (mTLS gateway | VPN | direct connect).
- Soojin/Monica: we'll schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the matrix with your security team.
